I have been farming these 20 mu in Quzhou for 30 years, and I know this land like the back of my hand. It is just my husband and me, so we must be practical—20 mu of cotton is enough to keep us busy and put food on the table. Every year I start by rotary tilling the soil after the last frost to make a good seedbed. I will plant improved cotton seeds in late April because the traditional varieties do not yield enough and hybrids are too expensive and hard to find here. I will put down compound fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium at planting, then top-dress with urea twice during the growing season for nitrogen. With my well, I can irrigate four times: once before sowing to ensure germination, once at flowering, once during boll setting, and a final time in late summer if the weather turns dry. Cotton bollworm and aphids always come, so I will spray pesticides five times, starting when the seedlings emerge and continuing through peak summer. After three decades, I expect about 260 kg of seed cotton per mu if the weather cooperates.
